exercise.name: Decline Sit-Up
steps: Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back.
Cross your arms and sit up until your chest is close to your knees.
Lower yourself back down slowly and with control.
exercise.one_line_summary: Feet hooked on a 20 deg decline bench, arms crossed on the chest. Start lying back on the pad; end sat up with the chest close to the knees (trunk about 16 deg past vertical, spine curled ~40 deg). Abs are the target; hip flexors help.

setup.target: Pad tilted 20 deg, high end 0.80 m, the head end lower than the feet.
setup.why: Library step 1: feet hooked under the pads of a decline bench; the slope makes the trunk lift against more of gravity than on the floor.

setup.target: Knees bent over the knee roll, ankles under the front roller.
setup.tolerance: feet stay under the roller in both pictures
setup.why: Library step 1. Hooked feet let the hip flexors pull, which S1 shows as high rectus femoris in the bent-knee sit-up.

setup.target: Arms crossed on the chest, fists on the chest.
setup.tolerance: forearms on the chest, not pulling the head
setup.why: Library step 2 (sit-up); crossed arms keep the hands off the neck.

movement.measure: root rot X; -110 = lying on the 20 deg pad
movement.end: sat up, shoulders ~16 deg forward of vertical
movement.path: Rolls up off the pad, upper back first, until the chest is near the knees.
Spine rounds as the trunk rises.

movement.start: bent over the roll, feet hooked

muscles.emg: Bent-knee sit-up among the highest exercises for the obliques; crunch highest for RA (S1). Eccentric sit-up raised abdominal EMG most (S2).
muscles.role: Main mover: curls and lifts the trunk.
muscles.surface: The two vertical bands down the front of the belly, lower ribs to the pubic bone.

muscles.emg: Greatest for the crunch and bent-knee sit-up (S1).
muscles.role: Helps the curl; not the target, not lit.
muscles.surface: Sides of the waist from the lower ribs to the hip bone.

muscles.emg: Rectus femoris highest in the bent-knee sit-up (S1); sit-ups raise hip-flexor EMG (S2).
muscles.role: Pulls the trunk up from the hips once the curl is done; not lit (the app lists abs only).
muscles.surface: Front of the hip and the top of the thigh.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Fingers laced behind the neck, chin yanked down.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Strains the neck; library step 2 says arms crossed.

sources.citation: Escamilla RF, McTaggart MS, Fricklas EJ, et al. 2006. An electromyographic analysis of commercial and common abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 36(2):45-57. doi:10.2519/jospt.2006.36.2.45
sources.what_it_gave: Upper/lower rectus abdominis greatest in the crunch (with Ab Slide, Torso Track); obliques greatest in the crunch and bent-knee sit-up; rectus femoris greatest in the bent-knee sit-up.

sources.citation: Kim K, Lee T. 2016. Comparison of muscular activities in the abdomen and lower limbs while performing sit-up and leg-raise. J Phys Ther Sci 28(2):491-494. doi:10.1589/jpts.28.491
sources.what_it_gave: Sit-up vs leg raise (upper/lower RA, external oblique, rectus femoris, iliopsoas): the eccentric sit-up raised abdominal activity most; the leg raise and eccentric sit-up raised hip-flexor activity.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
sources.what_it_gave: Erector spinae highest in back extensions (~63% MVIC on the floor, ~56% on a bench); V-sits ~80% MVIC rectus abdominis; adding a stability ball raises core EMG; sit-ups and curl-ups the classic core exercises.
The steps the app shows; the pictures must match them.

clip_check.check: Start: back and head on the pad
End: chest close to the knees
Feet hooked under the roller in both
